prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1459; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured's representing attorney's office reporting a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Claimant is represented, so all contact will route through counsel going forward.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy declarations and confirmed the driver involved is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and records the same general sequence of events the claimant described.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the accident happened as described and had no disagreement about how the vehicles came together.

Entry 5: Collected three witness statements and several scene photos. All of them line up with the claimant's account of the impact.

Entry 6: Inspected the claimant's vehicle. The damage pattern is consistent with the impact described, and there is no sign of earlier damage to the same areas.

Entry 7: Ran a prior-claims search and found no earlier injury claims or treatment involving the same body area for this claimant.

Entry 8: Counsel sent the initial injury report describing neck strain. The reported symptoms fit the kind and force of this collision well.

Entry 9: Claimant's recorded statement was taken through counsel. Several small details were added compared with the first account, but the core story did not change.

Entry 10: Medical records show a treatment course running somewhat longer than is typical for a neck strain of this kind. Requested the provider's notes to understand the timeline of visits.

Entry 11: Reviewed the provider notes and billing with the medical reviewer. The treatment is documented and linked to the reported injury, and the length of care is noted for the file.

Entry 12: Current status: liability and coverage are accepted, the vehicle damage is recorded, and the injury evaluation is ongoing with counsel. Next step is to finalize the medical review before setting an offer.
